chapter: Records and the Don Albert band
title: Louis Cottrell in his band and Cottrell's father the drummer
summary: Russell relays Cottrell's years with the band; Albert recalls Cottrell's father carrying his drums on his back.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Is there anything you can tell us about the vocalian records you made under your own name? Oh, by the way, another man I saw, I met on the street the day before I left, that was on Monday, is Louis Cottrell, the clarinetist. Sure. He's president of the union now. That's correct. And also an insurance collector or something. That's right. He was going down St. Peter's Street, and as I walked out of my door, and I was in a hurry, he said, I'm going over to Texas, and I hope to see one of your old friends over there. And I said, tell him hello for me.
Well, here's his name right here.
He was one of the, he was an original member in my band.
I said, how long were you with the band? He said, oh, nine years. He gave the date, something like up to 1938 or something. I forget. That's right.
This is Cottrell's, Cottrell's daddy was a great drummer.
Yes, we've, a lot of people have told us about him.
Oh, he was great. I used to love to see him come in in the morning with his drum strapped on his back. That's how they carried the drums.
Well, he did? I didn't notice. The bass drum? The bass drum on the back and snare drum in his hand. You know, some people tell us about one time he had a collapsible drum that folded up.
I don't remember that. Made out of something like aluminum, something like. I think I recall that. I never did see one myself.
I think I recall that. Not positive. I want to say for sure that I do. But offhand, I do remember him carrying a small package.
